for_the_director.what: The redesigned value test (docs/design/THE_VALUE_TEST_REDESIGN.md, 16d90c311) leaves two choices that define what "beating a flat supplier" means. First, for the standard-variable pair, whether the flat baseline charges the price cap. Second, whether the result is ever reduced to one number by weighing money against time, carbon and peace of mind, or is reported only as the vector.
for_the_director.proposal: The standard-variable pair's flat arm charges the cap, and the efficient-supplier allowance arm (rule 4) stays the primary baseline. The result is reported as the M3 vector, with no weighting between axes. Where one arm wins on one axis and loses on another, the page says so in words and declares no winner.
for_the_director.recommendation: I recommend this. Evidence: an average GB supplier puts its standard-variable households on the cap. So a cap baseline is the "average player" the thesis names, while the efficient allowance tests whether the gain is more than a margin transfer (M2: "charging someone the cap transfers value rather than creating any"). M3 says each need is "measured in its own unit and never converted to pounds", which rules out a weighting I could choose. The trade-off is that a vector with mixed signs gives no headline verdict, and that is the honest reading. Holding position until he rules: steps 1 to 5 go ahead, both baselines are built, and nothing is weighted. What would change it: his ruling that a different flat supplier is the comparator, or a weighting he sets.

the_number_the_programme_rests_on.statement: WE CANNOT TELL. The headline figure of +0.5760 is the winner of a 45-way search, and when the SAME search is re-run against 200 shuffled worlds -- households' true sensitivities dealt out at random -- the winner reaches +0.5806 at the 95th percentile and matched or beat the real figure in 12 of them (p=0.0647). The measurement cannot separate this ceiling from chance, so we report no ceiling.
the_number_the_programme_rests_on.what_it_does_not_say: This is not a finding that price sensitivity is unlearnable. It is a refusal to distinguish, which is a different claim. The pair rung carries 69 households, and at that size only a ceiling above +0.5806 can be told from chance at all -- so a real effect of moderate size is invisible to this instrument either way. The separate full-coverage rung (n=164) reads cannot tell on the same correction, and the two rungs disagreeing is itself a reason to hold the number loosely. And the winning fit scores 0.5760 on households it never saw against 0.1977 on the ones it was built from -- 2.9 times better out of sample than in it. A fit does not do that; a search over 45 candidates ranked by the out-of-sample score finds one that does. This is not evidence the ceiling is chance -- the winner of a shuffled world overshoots its own fit for the same reason -- so the p-value above stands. It is the one thing that p-value cannot see, and it is why this figure is reported as the best of a search rather than as a bound. AND THE SIZE OF IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is a separate claim from whether it is real. +0.5760 is the largest of a search ranked on the very fold it is then reported from, so it is biased up as an estimate however cleanly it clears a null. De-biasing it needs a third fold — fit on one, choose on a second, score on a third — and this rung cannot carry one: 5.0 households per cell on the fit fold against the 8 this instrument requires. Forced through anyway it reads -0.0452, inside a noise floor of +0.2701 (p=0.7761) — the direction of travel, and not an estimate. The full-coverage rung CAN carry the split, and there the estimate is +0.2992, above its own noise floor of +0.1557 (p=0.005). Holding the fit fold at the same size and separating ONLY the choosing from the reporting moves the figure from +0.3362 to -0.0452, so +0.3814 of it is the search and nothing else — one variable, measured, not inferred. The rotations do not even agree on which candidate wins, and their estimates run from -0.3686 to +0.1446: which pair is 'best' is a fact about who landed on the ranking side of the split. So this rung can neither separate R1's ceiling from chance nor put an unbiased size on it. A49 gates R3 and R4 on this instrument and must read the magnitude field, which is null — not +0.5760. AND MORE COVERAGE CANNOT CLOSE THIS RUNG, which is the correction to what this sentence used to say. Its population is not the book's: it is set by whichever pair wins, and the winner reaches through a field the company holds only where a renewal fired, so the rung collapses to the renewing subset however large the book grows. The SAME search restricted to the fields the company holds on every account on supply does carry the split — on all 164 households — and there the magnitude is +0.2513 against its own noise floor of +0.1628 (p=0.01). That is a NARROWER claim over a different population, not a better draw of this one, and it is published beside this rung rather than instead of it.

the_number_the_programme_rests_on.why_both_figures_are_shown: The first number is what a search of 45 candidate pairs returned, compared against the odds of ONE of them coming up by chance. The second compares it against the odds of the BEST OF ALL of them coming up by chance, which is the thing that actually happened. Both are shown because deleting the flattering one would hide that it was ever published.

the_most_a_carbon_score_could_be_worth.bound_kind_reason: TRUE CEILING. Perfect foreknowledge of the half-hourly intensity shape is exactly the quantity a real forecast approximates, and perfect compliance is exactly what advice approximates, so no buildable method beats `hindsight_ceiling`. A reading at or below the null therefore RETIRES the time-shifting candidate outright, which is what a floor could never do.
the_most_a_carbon_score_could_be_worth.bound_scope: The TIMING lever on ELECTRICITY only. A negative here retires nothing about consumption reduction, physical measures or gas.
not_bounded_by_this: reduction -- using less. Abates both kWh and carbon and is R4's subject.
gas -- a near-constant factor per kWh burned. It emits when burned, so no timing benefit exists and none is claimed (scope brief §B).
physical measures -- efficiency, solar, heat pumps. R4's subject, and bounded there.
tariff switching -- moves money, never carbon. The director's standing rule: savings count only from reduced or time-shifted usage, never from discounting.
embodied carbon in any measure or asset fitted.

rebound -- part of a saving returns as extra comfort. It cannot reduce a TIMING ceiling (the kWh is unchanged), which is why it is out of scope here and in scope for every reduction figure R4 reports.
the_most_a_carbon_score_could_be_worth.trend_reads: UNDERSTATES the real-day figure -- averaging days flattens within-day spread. It is carried for the TREND, not for the level.
the_most_a_carbon_score_could_be_worth.carbon_value_basis: DESNZ traded carbon values 2025, Table 1, central case, real 2025 GBP
named_gaps: SHIFTABLE SHARE of domestic load. Nothing in the knowledge layer, the commons or the market research establishes one, so the headline is reported at share = 1.0 and the curve is published instead of a figure. This is the single number that would turn the ceiling into an estimate, and it is a question to research.
The non-traded (appraisal) carbon value is held only as an asserted anchor (~£80-90/tCO2e). Sourcing it would roughly double every money figure above.
Book depth (A46): every figure here is a per-year rate over a book whose renewal history is thin, so what a ceiling can be DEMONSTRATED over is bounded separately.

The shape is exogenous: a book-wide shift would itself move the merit order. At 164 households against ~28M GB homes that is negligible, and at national scale it is not -- which makes this a ceiling for THIS company and not for the policy.
caveats: Computed over 20 whole days in years 2016, 2021, 2022, 2025. That is a small panel and the figure carries its sample size for that reason.

The typical-day cross-check below understates within-day spread because averaging days flattens it; the real-day rungs overstate it by the measured factor. The two bracket the answer rather than agreeing.
the_most_a_carbon_score_could_be_worth.statement: R3's timing ceiling CLEARS its null by 4.82x, so there is real carbon in the grid's shape for a score to point at. At perfect foreknowledge, perfect compliance and EVERY kWh moved, the whole 68-household book abates 10.68 tCO2e/yr -- £6.91 per household-year at the DESNZ traded carbon value. Acting on a real forecast and correcting the shape's own measured within-day exaggeration takes that to £4.03 per household-year (91.7 kgCO2e). Those are CEILINGS at a shiftable share of 1.0, which no household has; at a tenth of load moved the figure is a tenth of that. And it is shrinking: on the typical-day series the headroom moved -42.1% between 2016 and 2025 as the grid decarbonised, so the programme is worth less every year it is not built.

the_most_the_products_beyond_price_could.bound_kind: MIXED — declared per product, and the split IS the finding
the_most_the_products_beyond_price_could.bound_kind_reason: A49 requires each instrument to state whether it is a true CEILING (a negative retires the candidate outright) or a handicapped FLOOR (a negative retires nothing). the_most_the_products_beyond_price_could.refuses_to_total: There is no total here and that is deliberate. The products are NOT disjoint (advice is the channel for the others; solar and a heat pump both change grid import) and the columns are NOT one currency (tariff fit's pounds are a bill saving, time-shifting's are carbon valued at the traded price). A sum would double-count across products and add two quantities across currencies, and it is the number a reader would quote.
the_most_the_products_beyond_price_could.why_time_shifting_has_no_pounds: R3's pounds are CARBON VALUED at the traded price, not a bill saving. A shifted kWh is cheaper only on a time-of-use tariff and this book holds none, so the BILL saving from shifting is zero here and the carbon value sits in its own column. Adding it to tariff fit's pounds would sum two different quantities.

the_sharing_ceiling.why_it_is_not_added_to_this_arm: It is a COUNTERFACTUAL about a product that does not exist, and this arm reports what THIS book can do. Adding it would publish a bill saving no household on this book can receive. It is carried beside the None so the size of the missing product is visible: the gap is not a rounding error, it is the largest bounded figure in R4.
the_sharing_ceiling.and_only_this_column_can_be_shared: The carbon lands on nobody's bill, so no tariff can share it. The money does. That makes the tariff the PRECONDITION for the abatement rather than a way of monetising it -- the money is what pays for the behaviour that abates.
the_sharing_ceiling.the_optimum_is_interior: The company's own take is zero at BOTH ends of the frontier, so for any shift response that increases with pass-through its maximum is STRICTLY INTERIOR. That conclusion needs no elasticity and none is asserted: it follows from the two endpoints alone.
the_sharing_ceiling.where_the_optimum_sits: Where the interior optimum is. That needs the shift response as a function of pass-through, and nothing in the knowledge layer, the commons or the market research establishes one. It is a question to research, not a number to pick.
the_sharing_ceiling.why_the_frontier_ROWS_are_not_published_: The frontier holds the created value FIXED, so its rows are conditional on the shift happening at all. Its zero-pass-through row therefore reads `company keeps the whole ceiling`, and that is not a take anyone could bank: at zero pass-through a household's bill is identical whenever it draws, so nothing moves and nothing is created. Published as a row it would read as value the company could keep for doing nothing -- value TRANSFERRED dressed as value CREATED, which is the one substitution the mission forbids. So the identity travels with the endpoints that bound it and never alone.

named_gaps: PROPERTY ATTRIBUTES. Nothing in the book distinguishes one home's fabric, roof or heating system from another's. This is the single acquisition that would turn three FLOORS into CEILINGS, and it is a data question rather than a modelling one.

That is a product decision, and it is what would let the household share in the value R3 measures. the_most_the_products_beyond_price_could.statement: R4 SPLITS, AND THE SPLIT IS THE ANSWER. Of six products, 3 are true CEILINGS and 3 are FLOORS (efficiency_fabric, solar, heat_pump) -- because the property-attribute census over 29 logs found 0 attributes, so a measure cannot be sized for a specific home and a negative would retire nothing. THE PART WE CAN BOUND IS THE PART THAT CANNOT ABATE: tariff fit is worth £2.19 per household-year and its carbon ceiling is EXACTLY ZERO by the director's own rule, because discounting moves money and changes no kWh and no hour. The part that abates -- time-shifting, at 91.7 kgCO2e per household-year -- carries no bill saving at all, because this book holds no time-of-use tariff for a shifted kWh to be cheaper on. So the canon's charge is confirmed by arithmetic rather than by assertion: the company can make a household cheaper and never greener. AND BOTH BOUNDED ARMS ARE SMALL: £2.19 of bill saving and £4.03 of carbon value per household-year, only 7 of 68 households priced above the market reference at all. So the whole of the part of R4 this book can bound is worth a few pounds a household-year, and any real value in the programme lives in the arms that are FLOORS. R4 IS NOT RETIRED -- nothing here bounds the measures from above -- but what stands between it and a bound is a DATA ACQUISITION, not a model.
